clue.text: Novel idiot, when announced, gets unlimited votes

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like a synonym of idiot

parts.note: a donkey is a fool or idiot; said in the plural, 'donkeys' gives the sound of the first part

indicators.note: without limits means the first and last letters of votes are dropped

explanation.surface: A foolish candidate somehow wins an endless number of votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when announced' says DONKEYS is heard rather than spelt: it sounds like DONQUIX, the British way of saying the first part of the title. 'unlimited' strips V and S from 'votes', leaving OTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cervantes's famous book about a deluded knight is a classic Spanish novel.

clue.text: Vacant Eros is holding up contraceptive …

indicators.note: holding means the emptied word wraps round the next piece
vacant means emptied, so only the first and last letters of Eros remain
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the pill is the common contraceptive

explanation.surface: The statue of Eros, gone blank, holds up a contraceptive and trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the printed dots themselves, a three-dot mark. 'up' turns PILL to LLIP, which 'holding' puts inside ES (Eros 'Vacant').
explanation.definitionFit: The row of three dots marking an omission or a trailing-off sentence is called by this punctuation name.

clue.text: I slip up, going north east without bearing

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the word is written upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: to slip up is to err, make a mistake
the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean region, literally the land where the sun rises

explanation.surface: A traveller confesses to a stumble while heading north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going north' turns ERR into RRE. Levant comes from the French for 'rising', so it is a name for the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no bearing on a matter has no relevance to it.

clue.text: Served up very fine sole?

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the whole piece is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: too can mean very, as in 'not too bad'
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades

explanation.surface: A diner is presented with an exquisite piece of sole fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served up' turns TOO + F round. The question mark flags the definition by example: the sole is the underside of the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The sole is the underside of this body part, so the clue defines it by one of its parts.

clue.text: Stravinsky's contribution to Ruddigore

definitions.note: the clue means Stravinsky's given name, the possessive pointing to what belongs to him

indicators.note: a contribution to something is a part of it, so the letters come from inside Ruddigore

explanation.surface: A famous Russian composer is said to have had a hand in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruddigore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera; the composer's first name sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor was the given name of the Russian composer of The Rite of Spring.

clue.text: Fancies girl in many ways

indicators.note: in means the girl's name is placed inside the directions

parts.note: E, N and S are compass points, several directions or ways one can go
Joy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone takes a liking to a young woman in all sorts of ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many ways' gives several compass points, E, N and S, a common crossword reading of directions.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to like it or take pleasure in it.

clue.text: Summoned up god

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to be sued is to be summoned to court

explanation.surface: A deity is called upon from below.
explanation.definitionFit: Deus is Latin for a deity.

clue.text: Flatten bagel, say

definitions.meaning: to flatten ground or pastry by passing a cylinder over it
a bagel is one kind of bread bun

explanation.definitionFit: Rolling a lawn or dough flattens it, and a bagel is a type of bread bun.

clue.text: Spice girl's debut also held back by lookalike

indicators.note: held means the reversed piece is gripped inside the lookalike word

parts.note: a ringer is someone who looks just like another, a dead ringer

indicators.note: back means those letters run in reverse order
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter of girl's is taken

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl's first show is also upstaged by an impersonator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns G + TOO into OOTG; 'held ... by' sets that inside RINGER. The Spice Girls surface is a red herring for the spice itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The fresh rhizome of the ginger plant, used whole in cooking, is a familiar spice.

clue.text: European fruit about to be exported by Arabs, say?

definitions.note: Arabs here are a breed of horse; the clue gives an example, and the answer is the adjective describing them

indicators.note: exported means sent out, so the letter is removed from the fruit

parts.note: a quince is a hard yellow fruit
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A Continental fruit is shipped abroad by Middle Eastern traders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be exported' takes C out of QUINCE. 'Arabs' are a breed of horse, not people, and the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Arab horses are a breed of the horse family, which this adjective describes.

clue.text: One walking slowly on hill is shrouded in legend?

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: shrouded in means the word is wrapped inside the next piece

parts.note: read as leg-end: the end of a leg is a toe

explanation.surface: A slow hiker on a hilltop has become the stuff of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' is split as leg-end, giving TOE; 'shrouded in' puts IS inside it. 'on' sets that after TOR. A tor is a craggy hill in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile famous for its slow plodding gait, as in the fable of the race with the hare.

clue.text: Recordings of diamonds being hidden by force

indicators.note: being hidden by means the suit letter sits inside the word for force

parts.note: vis is Latin for force or strength
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: Video evidence shows jewels being concealed by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: VIS, Latin for force, is used in English phrases such as vis viva.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for videos, informal for recorded clips.

clue.text: Steroid rolled with joint that's given to top hack

indicators.note: rolled means the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A drug cocktail with a spliff is handed to the senior journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' rearranges STEROID into EDITORS. 'joint' looks like a cannabis cigarette but is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior post on a newspaper, run by the chief journalist, is that publication's top job.

clue.text: One married mum and I go away!

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
mum means silent, and sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A married mother and her child are told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' means keep quiet, not mother. The answer is old British Army slang, from Arabic, for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang command borrowed by soldiers from Arabic, telling someone to leave.

clue.text: Rainbow-coloured light under old bouquet

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the light piece is placed below the old piece

parts.note: pale means light in colour
a wine's bouquet is its scent

explanation.surface: A shimmering lamp sits beneath an old bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests flowers but means aroma, as of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing a milky play of shifting colours, like the gemstone opal.

clue.text: Catherine wheel finally worked free

indicators.note: worked means the letters have been reshaped into a new order
finally means only the last letter of wheel is used

explanation.surface: A spinning firework finally comes loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges CATHERINE plus L, the last letter of 'wheel'. A Catherine wheel is a spinning firework, a staple of Bonfire Night in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone no longer under suspicion or in danger is clear of trouble, at liberty.

clue.text: They're charged by knight in ten seconds

indicators.note: in means the knight letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, making ten
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is accused, all within ten seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is ten written as digits; N is the knight in chess notation, since K is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms carrying an electric charge are the particles defined here.

clue.text: Oddly enough, Altman's introducing final parts of Paradise Lost

indicators.note: introducing means the end letters are brought inside the odd letters
oddly means the odd-numbered letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the final two letters of Paradise are S and E

explanation.surface: Strangely, the film director Altman brings in the closing scenes of Milton's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly enough' keeps A, T, A from ALTMAN; 'introducing' slips SE inside. 'Paradise Lost' is the title of Milton's poem, but 'Lost' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being confused or bewildered, as a ship without bearings on the ocean.

clue.text: Volunteers put on abandoned Kola Peninsula for eastern exercise

indicators.note: put on means the volunteers come after the first piece in an across answer
abandoned means emptied out, so only the first and last letters of the phrase remain

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers are sent to a deserted Russian peninsula for training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' empties 'Kola Peninsula', leaving K and A. The TA (Territorial Army) is the British volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A set sequence of moves practised in Japanese martial arts such as karate is a form of drill.

clue.text: Jumper/anorak go badly together

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put together in a disordered way

explanation.surface: A sweater and a rain jacket clash when worn as one outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ANORAK and GO. 'Jumper' suggests a British sweater beside the anorak, but it is a hopping animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial famous for hopping is a leaping animal.

clue.text: Via live TV, Peel broadcast soft material

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: John Peel's show goes out live on television featuring plush fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges LIVE, TV and PEEL. John Peel was a famous BBC radio DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric with a short, dense, raised nap, smooth to the touch.

clue.text: Joined shovel and crowbar with this?

definitions.text: Joined shovel and crowbar with this?

indicators.note: joined means the tail of shovel is fastened onto the next piece
with means the start of crowbar is taken along with it

explanation.surface: A tool-shed puzzle: what fastener could hold a spade and a jemmy together?
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'shovel' joined to the start of 'crowbar' spells the answer, and the whole clue also asks what would fasten the two tools.
explanation.definitionFit: The hook-and-loop fastening tape is used to stick objects together.

clue.text: Northern wee, round vegetable

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: wee and pee are both informal words for urine

explanation.surface: A small Northern root vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wee' looks like Scots for small but means urine; 'round' turns PEE back to EEP. The answer is Scots for a turnip or swede.
explanation.definitionFit: Scottish dialect name for a swede or turnip, eaten with haggis.

clue.text: Once left out by the deck

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Once someone is left out, they sit by the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ONCE plus L. 'deck' is the verb meaning dress, not part of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck is to dress or adorn, as in decking a hall, which means clothing it.

clue.text: Inner ear cleaned out regularly? Not at all

indicators.note: regularly cleaned out means every other letter is removed, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: Is the inner ear given a regular clean? Never.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaned out regularly' removes I, N, R, A, keeping the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic contraction of never, meaning at no time at all.

clue.text: Time to influence diplomacy

parts.note: to act on something is to influence it

explanation.surface: It is time to sway things by diplomatic means.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensitivity in handling people without giving offence is a diplomatic skill.

clue.text: The Lion'sheart taken by a Lamb

indicators.note: heart means the central letters of the phrase The Lion are taken

explanation.surface: In the biblical image, the lion's heart is taken by a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of THE LION (dropping T and ON) gives ELI; 'taken by' adds A. Charles Lamb, the essayist, wrote as Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: The pen name used by the English essayist Charles Lamb for his essays.

clue.text: Gently hold pet lamb, grasping both sides

indicators.note: grasping means the lamb word holds the side letters within it
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a cade is a lamb reared by hand as a pet
R for right and L for left are the two sides
R for right and L for left are the two sides

explanation.surface: Tenderly hug a hand-reared lamb, clasping it on each side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' puts R (right) and L (left) inside CADE, each at its own spot. CADE is an old word for a hand-reared lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something protectively in the arms, as one would a baby in a cot.

clue.text: Deflecting about half, say

definitions.note: deflecting is a gerund, the act of bending; the answer is the noun for that act

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a half is an example of a fraction

explanation.surface: Turning aside roughly half of something, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half, say' defines by example: a half is one fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: The bending of light or sound as it passes into a new medium.

clue.text: Star of Dr Zhivago, film hero returns missing book

indicators.note: missing means a letter is left out
returns means the hero's name runs backwards

parts.note: Rambo is the action-film hero played by Sylvester Stallone

explanation.surface: An action hero returns to the screen without his script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RAMBO into OBMAR; 'missing' then drops B.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Sharif played the title role in the 1965 film of Pasternak's novel.
